In other news, Node 11.2 is live on the mainnet and has brought core upgrade features. AMBCrypto reported that node configs came in a new “envelope” format that nodes older than 11.2 would not be able to read, which means operators will have to upgrade.

Despite the news, the price reaction has been minimal so far.

The MVRV ratio measures how much profit or loss the average investor is sitting on. Santiment data also tracks MVRV data across different rolling timeframes, such as 30-day (short-term holder) and 180-day (long-term holder).

The data showed that both the 30-day and 180-day MVRV ratios were below zero. In other words, these holders were facing losses, on average, of 15.21% and 8.9%, respectively.

The September rally saw the MVRV ratios reach highly positive territory, especially for the 180-day cohort. It was expected that this would prompt profit-taking and selling pressure. The sustained ADA price losses below $0.20 were also due to crypto market-wide fear as Bitcoin faced rejection below $80k.

The daily active addresses numbers have tumbled compared to levels registered in the first half of October too, from a peak of 29k to just 12k-14k in recent days.

The price correction to $0.194 in mid-September saw the 2-year dormant circulation spike, and also caused a minor dip in the 2-year mean coin age.

These metrics measure the amount of tokens not transacted for a specific period of time, and the average number of days all ADA tokens were in their addresses, in a rolling window of the chosen time period (for example, 90 days).

Over the past six weeks, while Cardano was in steady decline, both the 90-day and 2-year MCA have trended higher. Meanwhile, the dormant circulation was relatively quiet.

This relative quiet was markedly different from the panicked offloading seen in June. Back then, Cardano prices were crashing towards the $0.14-$0.15 lows. Dormant circulation was high, and the mean coin age was in freefall.

Therefore, despite the steady drawdown in recent weeks, the sentiment was likely quite different, as the evidence at hand shows.

#5208. Forget ‘Ultrasound Money’? Vitalik Buterin Pushes New Ethereum Store-of-Value Vision

Ethereum co-creator Vitalik Buterin is challenging one of Ether’s most celebrated investment narratives, suggesting that the second-largest crypto’s long-term value should depend less on how many tokens the network burns and more on its ability to become a reliable store of value.

The remarks could signal a major shift in how Ethereum’s value proposition is presented, particularly as declining transaction-fee burns weaken the deflationary narrative that once made ETH attractive to investors.

In a Sunday morning post on X, Buterin outlined three main reasons for shifting attention away from Ethereum’s fee-burning narrative and toward its potential as a store of value.

First, he argued that ETH’s deflationary appeal was never as powerful as it seemed. Although the 2021 EIP-1559 upgrade introduced a mechanism to burn a portion of transaction fees, the amount of ETH destroyed has not always been enough to offset new token issuance. In his view, making fee burns the central measure of Ethereum’s success places too much emphasis on a single aspect of its token economics. According to Buterin, even if fee burns remain below 10% of the level required to offset new issuance indefinitely, Buterin said, “we should not feel sad,” adding that “the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.”

Another concern is that prioritizing ETH as a fee-burning asset could push Ethereum toward decisions that undermine its core principles. Buterin suggested that designing the network primarily to maximize transaction-fee burns could create tensions with decentralization and censorship resistance. Such an approach could require trade-offs that make the network less open and less resistant to external control, potentially weakening the very qualities that distinguish Ethereum from competing blockchain networks.

Notably, the fee-burning mechanism was central to Ethereum’s popular “ultrasound money” narrative, which gained significant traction among ETH investors during the 2021 bull run. The thesis suggested that by permanently removing a portion of transaction fees from circulation, Ethereum could become increasingly deflationary, potentially making ETH scarcer and more valuable over time.

He also sees an opportunity in the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence. As AI continues to disrupt industries and reshape economic activity, dependable financial infrastructure could become more valuable. “In the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued,” he wrote.

Buterin believes Ethereum’s emphasis on stability could give ETH a stronger store-of-value proposition in this changing environment, shifting the investment narrative away from token burns and toward the network’s ability to preserve trust over the long term.

Interestingly, Buterin’s position also found support from Solana co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko, who appeared to share his skepticism about making transaction fees the centerpiece of a blockchain’s value proposition. Yakovenko dismissed the idea of treating fees as the product, calling it “absolutely meaningless.” He argued that blockchain networks should focus on delivering tangible value to users rather than trying to control how much people pay to have their transactions included in a block.

#5207. XRP Ledger Introduces Quantum-Proof Security Upgrade to Users

As the XRP Ledger developers continue to make committed efforts to make the network fully quantum-resistant in the coming year, the team has just proposed a major upgrade that has sparked a buzz across the XRP community.

Sparking fresh excitement across the XRP community earlier today, the XRP Ledger (XRPL) Foundation has disclosed plans to introduce quantum-resistant accounts to users.

The team revealed plans to introduce a new feature to the XRP Ledger to offer users strict protection against future quantum computing threats without paying additional transaction fees.

While it is yet to be implemented, the proposed design will allow users to add a NIST-approved ML-DSA-44 signing key to their accounts and disable their existing keys.

This way, it will become harder for potential quantum attacks to compromise accounts, especially those whose public keys have already been exposed.

Apart from the extra layer of protection the upgrade promises to offer users, its cost-effective design has stirred more interest among the XRP community.

Notably, users will not have to pay higher transaction fees to access the additional security, as the proposed feature allows XRP holders to strengthen their account protection without worrying about extra transaction costs.

The proposed upgrade sends relief across the crypto ecosystem as it addresses concerns about the possibility of increasingly powerful quantum computers eventually breaking some of the cryptographic systems currently used to secure blockchains and cryptocurrencies.

While the upgrade is yet to launch, the team revealed that it has scheduled a migration study for the first half of 2027.

The study is aimed at examining how existing accounts can transition to the new security system and what the process would involve for users.

The proposed security upgrade has further sparked more optimism as it is also part of Ripple's broader aim of achieving full quantum protection by 2028.

#5206. Alta Raises $80 Million to Build the Infrastructure for Onchain Global Banking

Disclaimer: The below article is sponsored, and the views in it do not represent those of ZyCrypto. Readers should conduct independent research before taking any actions related to the project mentioned in this piece. This article should not be regarded as investment advice.

Alta, a financial infrastructure company building the foundation for the next generation of global finance, has announced $80 million in total funding — including a $47.5 million Series A round and $32.5 million in previous seed financing. The Series A was led by Index Ventures, with participation from GV (Google Ventures), Blackbird Ventures, Square Peg, and Capital 49.

The timing is deliberate. Alta’s launch comes as regulatory clarity improves and institutional demand for tokenized finance accelerates.

Today’s global financial system remains fragmented and riddled with inefficiency. Moving money across borders can take days, and institutions must hold substantial cash buffers to maintain liquidity across jurisdictions and payment networks. Globally, an estimated $4 trillion sits tied up in prefunded accounts.

Alta is building a more efficient alternative — combining instant settlement with global payment connectivity, foreign exchange, and treasury management in a single system.

At the core of Alta’s technology is a new blockchain architecture built on recursive zero-knowledge cryptography. It allows institutions to keep balances, transactions, identities, and compliance policies private — while still cryptographically proving that every transaction meets the required rules.

Designed to operate across assets, chains, and jurisdictions, Alta pairs programmable compliance with the controls and scalability that institutional finance and agentic commerce demand.

Leading financial platform Airwallex has chosen to build on Alta, connecting its global payments infrastructure with Alta’s blockchain technology. Beyond pay-ins and pay-outs via stablecoins, the collaboration will support connectivity to local fiat payment networks across 200 countries and 90 currencies.

That reflects Alta’s broader positioning: neutral infrastructure that banks, payment providers, and other financial institutions can all build on.

Alta’s first product is designed to help businesses manage liquidity more efficiently and free up the cash buffers trapped in prefunded accounts. Built on tokenized assets, it enables just-in-time funding and more efficient foreign exchange — and lets businesses move instantly in and out of yield-bearing tokenized assets, maximizing the interest earned on otherwise idle capital.

“With the rise of agentic banking and programmable payments, stablecoins are becoming an important vector for settlement. Financial institutions need blockchain infrastructure that is private, neutral, regulated, and connected to global fiat rails. Alta is building exactly that,” said Jack Zhang, Co-Founder of Alta and Co-Founder/CEO of Airwallex. “We’re proud to be an early design partner and help Alta deliver onchain finance at institutional scale.”

Alta’s investors bring together expertise across financial technology, enterprise infrastructure, and blockchain innovation.

“Loong is the sort of technologist you only meet a few times in a career. After a major fintech exit from his first company, he went on to run the largest supercomputing calculation in history at its time, then discovered a cancer drug now in human trials. With Catherine’s exceptional track record of bringing industry leaders to the table and Jack’s understanding of the problem space, this is a team we had to back,” said Jan Hammer, Partner at Index Ventures.

“The Alta founders have successfully built and scaled multi-billion-dollar technology and financial infrastructure businesses, and understand how to de-risk complex institutional execution. We have been impressed with their combination of deep-tech blockchain engineering, institutional go-to-market knowledge, and vision for scale, and we look forward to supporting them in their mission to reimagine financial infrastructure at its core,” said Tom Hulme, Managing Partner at GV.

The new funding will support continued development of Alta’s blockchain infrastructure, the expansion of its institutional partnerships and global financial connectivity, and the growth of its engineering and compliance teams.

A Bitcoin rally could create favorable conditions for MEMASA’s debut. The bigger test will be whether the app delivers on its promise to simplify crypto trading and attracts enough users to build lasting demand for its token.

Bitcoin’s next test is the support near $73,500. Holding it keeps a recovery toward $84,400 in play, while a break could send the price toward $70,000.

The long view looks calmer, as JPMorgan’s bull case still points to about $150,000 by the end of the decade, though with sharp swings along the way.

MEMASA faces a different test, as it needs to turn an AI trading concept into an app people use regularly. If it succeeds, demand for its utility token could grow with the ecosystem, and today’s $0.0155 sale price would become its reference point.

Both Bitcoin’s path and MEMASA’s outcome remain uncertain, and higher potential comes with higher risk.

#5203. XRP Ledger Unveils Fee-Free Quantum-Proof Upgrade as Ripple Races Toward 2028 Security Deadline: Here’s What’s Coming

The XRP Ledger is preparing for a major security overhaul as quantum computing moves from a theoretical concern to a growing priority for the crypto industry. With Ripple targeting 2028 for its post-quantum security transition, developers are now unveiling a proposed quantum-resistant upgrade that promises to protect users against future attacks without introducing additional transaction fees.

The development could mark a significant turning point for the network, raising questions about what exactly is changing, how the upgrade will work, and whether XRP holders will need to do anything before the looming security deadline.

The XRP community has a new development to watch as the XRP Ledger Foundation outlines plans to strengthen the network against future quantum computing risks. The proposed upgrade would introduce quantum-resistant accounts, giving users an additional layer of protection against emerging cryptographic threats while keeping transaction costs unchanged.

Although the feature has yet to be implemented, the proposed upgrade would allow XRP Ledger users to register NIST-approved ML-DSA-44 quantum-resistant signing keys and deactivate their existing authentication keys. This would give accounts an additional layer of protection against potential quantum computing attacks, particularly those whose public keys have already been exposed on the network.

Importantly, users could adopt the enhanced security system without changing how they store, hold, or access their XRP. The concern stems from how transactions are authorized on the network. When users sign transactions through their cryptocurrency wallets, their public keys can become exposed, potentially creating an attack vector if sufficiently advanced quantum computers emerge.

Such technology could eventually undermine existing cryptographic protections, putting accounts with exposed public keys at risk. The XRP Ledger Foundation’s proposed solution is designed to address this vulnerability before quantum computing advances to the point where such attacks become practically achievable.

Beyond the additional protection, the proposal has another notable selling point: affordability. Users would not have to pay higher transaction fees to benefit from the enhanced security. In other words, XRP holders could strengthen their accounts against emerging quantum threats without incurring additional transaction costs, making the proposed upgrade particularly appealing to the community.

Although the upgrade has not yet gone live, the team has outlined its next steps, with a migration study planned for the first half of 2027. The research will explore how existing XRPL accounts can move to the new quantum-resistant security framework, including the transition process and what account holders would need to do to adopt the upgraded protection.

Developers are also addressing discrepancies in how the proposed system generates cryptographic keys across its Python, JavaScript, and server implementations, a necessary step toward ensuring consistent and reliable performance across the network.

As ZyCrypto previously reported, Ripple has outlined a comprehensive four-phase roadmap to make the XRP Ledger, its decentralized Layer-1 blockchain, resistant to potential quantum computing attacks, with full quantum readiness targeted for 2028.

Just a few days after the U.S. Treasury took action to cut global crypto exchange MEXC off from the U.S. financial system, Binance has also announced strict regulatory actions against the exchange.

On Tuesday, November 10, Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange by volume, announced its immediate decision to halt all transfers involving MEXC and all its affiliated companies.

Binance released an official announcement earlier today, warning users that it has stopped all trading services related to MEXC following new concerns about its legitimacy.

While the restrictions were announced to take effect immediately, Binance explained that its move follows the recent decision by the U.S. Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) to designate MEXC as a Primary Money Laundering Concern.

As such, Binance has prohibited its users from directly or indirectly sending funds to, receiving funds from, or conducting transactions through Binance involving MEXC and its related entities.

The MEXC-affiliated entities mentioned by Binance include MEXC Global Limited, MEXC Estonia OÜ, MEXC Singapore Pte Ltd, MEXC Global Foundation Ltd, GIDA Technology AG, and several other companies and affiliates operating under the MEXC name.

Although MEXC is among the top 20 crypto exchanges in the world, FinCEN issued an order against MEXC on November 6, cutting the exchange off from the U.S. financial system amid recent fraud allegations.

Notably, the U.S. Treasury accused the exchange of facilitating at least $16 billion in illicit transactions tied to sanctions evasion and cybercrime and of defrauding people of their funds.

While Binance remains the first crypto exchange to take action in accordance with FinCEN’s rule, it appears that many other exchanges are lining up to take similar action.

#5198. XRP Ledger Roadmap Puts Quantum-Resistant Accounts on the Agenda for 2027

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: The XRP Ledger Foundation’s forward-looking protocol roadmap includes work on quantum-resistant account options, including study of ML-DSA-44. It is a proposal and research direction, not a completed network-wide switch or a claim that today’s XRP accounts are already quantum-safe.

Quantum computing is a long-term security issue for public blockchains because sufficiently capable future machines could threaten some widely used digital-signature algorithms. That is still a different proposition from saying a machine exists today that can drain conventional blockchain wallets at scale.

The XRP Ledger Foundation’s protocol roadmap brings the issue into focus for the XRP ecosystem. Its outline includes studying quantum-resistant accounts and a possible migration path, with work contemplated across 2027 and 2028. It references ML-DSA-44, a post-quantum digital-signature approach, as one of the technologies under consideration.

A blockchain account authorizes transactions with cryptographic signatures. Many existing chains use schemes designed against attacks possible with classical computers. A future sufficiently powerful quantum computer could change the cost of attacking some of those schemes.

An alternative such as ML-DSA belongs to a newer class of algorithms designed with that threat model in mind. Swapping or supplementing account signatures, however, is not as simple as changing the display on a wallet application. Networks must consider transaction size, verification costs, hardware support, compatibility and the safety of moving long-established accounts.

For a public ledger, the transition also has to work for people who hold funds without regularly interacting with the network. There may be years of old addresses, signing devices and applications to accommodate.

The published document is a planning signal. It does not show that quantum-resistant accounts have already been activated for all XRP holders, that a final migration process has been agreed or that any future change will be seamless.

The Foundation’s references to potential milestones should be read as targets subject to research, engineering and community governance. Proposals can be revised, postponed or rejected as new evidence emerges. They also might require tradeoffs on fees and transaction handling.

NewsBTC previously looked at Ripple and Project Eleven’s work on preparing the XRP Ledger for quantum risks. The new roadmap places that wider conversation into the context of protocol development. Researchers can test candidate mechanisms, but moving from a proof of concept to a production ledger is a separate and more demanding step.

Many organizations are exploring onchain payments and instruments that could remain active for years. Our recent reporting on Ripple Prime’s institutional derivatives work illustrates the sorts of sophisticated financial activities developing around digital infrastructure.

Institutions often plan systems with long operating lives. That makes the ability to transition cryptography without interrupting services an important design issue, even where the immediate attack risk is uncertain. Building a tested option early could be less disruptive than having to react under emergency conditions later.

The roadmap is not a near-term XRP price catalyst with a guaranteed delivery date. Nor is it an indication that holders must abandon their current wallets today. The more useful questions are whether a formal amendment is developed, how its security is reviewed and whether wallet and custody providers can support it safely.

Clear documentation and broad testing will matter as much as the underlying algorithm. A secure primitive can still be undermined by poor implementation or a badly designed migration.

The practical takeaway is that quantum resilience is becoming an explicit development priority. The timetable and engineering details, rather than speculative claims about future computers, are what deserve close scrutiny from here.

#5197. Why Is Crypto Crashing Today? Bitcoin Falls Below $73K as Zcash (ZEC) Leads Crypto Losses

Why is crypto crashing? A hot CPI report raised Fed hike bets. ZEC fell below $1,000, the worst of 20 large coins this week.

Why is crypto crashing on Wednesday, November 11? The sell-off that began with Tuesday’s hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation report has carried into today, and almost every major coin is lower.

Bitcoin (BTC) dropped below $73,000 on Tuesday, touching $72,727 on Binance, and now trades at about $73,800. Ether (ETH) briefly slipped to $2,006, while XRP and Solana (SOL) are down 2% to 3% in 24 hours. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, a daily gauge of market mood from 0 to 100, has fallen to 29.

The report changed what traders expect from the Federal Reserve. Bond yields jumped, and bets on a larger December rate hike nearly tripled within two hours.

One coin is falling much harder than the rest. Zcash (ZEC) is a cryptocurrency launched in 2016 that lets users hide the sender, the receiver and the amount of a payment. It dropped below $1,000 on Wednesday for the first time since September 5. ZEC now trades at about $966, down 15.4% in 24 hours and 24.8% in a week.

ZEC has been one of this year’s best performers. It rose from about $526 on January 1 to a closing high of $1,653 on September 26. We checked the 20 largest coins on Binance, and ZEC fell the most over both the day and the week, even though it is still up 89% in 2026.

Trader 0x8742 opened a 10x long on 18,000 $ZEC ($17.63M) and is now down over $2.8M.

Liquidation price: $895.46.https://t.co/azzt3xvmay pic.twitter.com/wczndt7doC

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 11, 2026

So why are the markets spooked, and why is ZEC taking the hardest hit?

Inflation came in hot. The consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% economists expected. Core prices, which leave out food and energy, rose 0.3% against a 0.2% forecast.

That reading crossed a line the Fed had drawn. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech hours before the report that core inflation of about 0.3% would make a half-point hike in December worth considering.

Traders took him at his word. On Polymarket, the odds of a hike of 0.5 percentage point or more in December went from 4.4% just before the report to 12.8% two hours later. They sit at 9.4% now, while a standard quarter-point hike is priced at 85.5%.

Higher rates hurt crypto in a simple way. They make cash and bonds pay more, so money flows out of riskier bets. On Tuesday, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield rose from 4.86% to 4.98%.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

ZEC had the most to give back. We compared the price changes of 20 large coins on Binance over the past week and since January 1.

When markets get nervous, traders tend to sell what has made them the most money. ZEC has fallen 41% from its September 26 closing high of $1,653.

Borrowed money made the drop faster. On Hyperliquid, ZEC fell from $1,199.20 to $965.79 in less than a day. Lookonchain counted 32 traders holding more than $1 million each in leveraged bets on a rising ZEC price. Of those, 27 are now losing money, with about $23.7 million in paper losses between them.

Sharp drops have not always lasted. Since January 2025, ZEC has fallen 12% or more in a single day 14 times on Binance. Seven days later, it was higher eight times, with a median gain of 6.5%.

EXPLORE: Fed Meeting Today: Traders Price a 95% Hold and a 79% December Hike. What Does It Mean for Crypto?

ZEC trades at about $966. It touched $961.07 on Wednesday, its lowest price since September 4.

On the daily chart, where each candle covers one day, ZEC has fallen below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $1,200.68. It is still above its 200-day EMA at $872.23.

For Bitcoin, the line to watch is Tuesday’s low of $72,727. Below that, $68,902, the August 20 low, is the next support.

So, why is crypto crashing? A hot inflation report raised the odds of a bigger Fed hike, and ZEC’s leveraged bulls are paying the most for it. A daily close back above $1,050 would be the first sign the selling is easing.

According to longtime SHIB community member Mazrael, since the SHIB deployer wallet went silent in October 2021, at least 137 scam tokens have falsely claimed that the SHIB deployer sent them the coins. The intent of scammers is to 'fake' Shiba Inu's pseudonymous founder, "Ryoshi," and the reason behind this is to appear legitimate: If "Ryoshi" sent it, people trust it.

Mazrael explains how this trick works: a token is just a program, and it keeps its own record of transfers. The scammer can write any address into that record as the sender. So these scammers write the SHIB deployer's address, and on Etherscan it looks like "Ryoshi" sent the token. However, the real SHIB deployer (0xB8f2…FA08) hasn't sent a single transaction since October 2021.

How scammers fake "Ryoshi" Since the SHIB deployer wallet went silent in October 2021, at least 137 scam tokens have pretended it sent them their coins. Why? To look legitimate. If "Ryoshi" sent it, people trust it. How the trick works: A token is just a program, and it keeps its own record of transfers. The scammer can write ANY address into that record as the sender. So they write the SHIB deployer's address, and on Etherscan it looks like "Ryoshi" sent you their token. But the deployer never signed anything. Click the transaction itself and look at "From". That's the wallet that really sent it, and it's never the SHIB deployer. The numbers: - 9,131+ fake transfers - 2,500+ wallets hit - 0 signed by the deployer Some of the fakes: APE, three "SHIBA INU2.0" tokens, ShibChain, SHIB DAO, METARUFFY, a token literally called "Ryoshi", Caw and Baby Caw, three fake "Shibarium" tokens (a year before the real one), "BONE2.0" and three "UNLEASHED DAO" tokens. Many got shilled by OGs and ex-admins as "Ryoshi-backed" to make them look legit. The real SHIB deployer (0xB8f2…FA08) hasn't sent a single transaction since October 2021. Always check who signed the transaction, not what the token says.

'The SHIB deployer never signed anything,' Mazrael stated, urging the crypto community to click on related token transactions and examine the "From" address, saying this is the wallet that sent it and was never the SHIB deployer.

Mazrael shared the numbers, outlining over 9,131 fake transfers, over 2,500 wallets hit, and zero signed by the SHIB deployer. He went on to name some of these fake tokens, adding that some of these tokens got promoted as "Ryoshi-backed" to make them look legitimate.

This disclosure warns crypto users to always check who signed the transaction, not what the token says.

In a separate post, Mazrael explained that nothing links the SHIB deployer address to any person.

The SHIB deployer (0xB8f2…FA08) only deployed one contract: SHIB, and it hasn't sent a single transaction since October 2021. It has no public signed message on record, either on-chain or on Etherscan.

LEASH, BONE, and TREAT each came from different deployers. Mazrael indicated that BONE's deployer is shiba-swap.eth, whereas LEASH came from '0xA221…1494,' the same key that deployed StarLink, whose own site names Woof Decentra as LEASH's developer. That key kept LEASH's rebase oracle, an admin key, for five years.

#5193. NEAR AI Discloses SGLang Security Incident and Revokes Exposed API Keys

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: NEAR AI has published a security incident report involving an SGLang vulnerability in legacy deployments. The company says it revoked exposed credentials and addressed the issue, while acknowledging that some requests could have been observed. Its findings distinguish confirmed exposure from data it has no evidence was accessed.

A security disclosure from NEAR AI highlights a familiar danger in the expanding AI-agent industry: sophisticated applications can inherit serious problems from the infrastructure they run on.

In a November 9 incident report, the organization described an SGLang remote-code-execution vulnerability affecting legacy deployment infrastructure. The investigation identified roughly 100 user details and 18 agents in the affected context, with two Cloud API keys exposed and subsequently revoked.

The company said there was no evidence that stored Private Chat content had been compromised. It also cautioned that some requests made on November 8 could potentially have been observed. Those are not contradictory statements: investigators may find no evidence of one category of access while being unable to rule out another.

AI applications are assembled from multiple components: model servers, request routers, authentication systems, logging and the user-facing product. SGLang is part of the infrastructure used to serve language models. A flaw at that level can create opportunities for attackers before a user ever interacts with an onchain wallet or signs a transaction.

Remote-code-execution issues can be particularly serious because they may allow an attacker to run unauthorized instructions in the affected environment. The scope of what follows depends on the privileges, network access and data available to that environment.

For readers, this means the incident should not be conflated with a vulnerability in the NEAR blockchain consensus rules or a general compromise of all NEAR wallets. The report concerns particular AI-serving infrastructure and its potential exposures.

According to the published account, the team investigated affected deployments, revoked the two exposed API keys, remediated the vulnerability and notified impacted parties. Those are necessary containment steps, though the effectiveness of remediation depends on whether other pathways remain open and whether credentials are rotated wherever they were used.

The report’s numerical counts also need careful interpretation. Approximately 100 user details and 18 agents do not mean 100 users lost funds or that every associated request was read. Exposure, confirmed access and financial loss are separate findings that should not be collapsed into one sensational claim.

Crypto firms are integrating AI into development, support, trading and operational workflows. An AI tool may eventually handle private business information even when it cannot directly sign onchain transactions. That raises the value of conventional safeguards: isolating services, limiting credentials, monitoring access and maintaining incident-response plans.

The broader institutional push toward blockchain infrastructure, including the NYSE’s tokenized-securities plans, depends on more than smart-contract security. Offchain services must also be robust. A well-audited ledger cannot compensate for a compromised application server.

Likewise, rising institutional attention to crypto assets, which NewsBTC tracks through developments such as Ether ETF flows, makes operational controls increasingly consequential. These links are contextual rather than a claim that those products were involved in this incident.

Affected users should rely on NEAR AI’s direct notifications and published guidance. Where they have used credentials in related services, reviewing access permissions and rotating keys is prudent. Users should not assume that ordinary NEAR wallet keys have been exposed simply because the company reported an infrastructure flaw.

The most important follow-up is a clear technical postmortem explaining affected versions, root cause and validation of the fixes. For companies building AI agents around finance, the episode is a reminder that infrastructure security and candid disclosure are both part of earning trust.

American stockbroker Peter Schiff has warned of an imminent Bitcoin crash following the 2026 U.S. midterm elections.

Speaking to his followers on X, the well-known economic and capital markets analyst warned of a potential Bitcoin plunge.

His remarks suggested that BTC is set to lose resilience due to recent events that have eroded investor confidence and pushed crypto prices lower.

Based on his market observation, the analyst noted that since the recently concluded 2026 midterm elections, U.S. stock markets have surged around 12% while Bitcoin dropped by 4.6%. Over the same period, gold and silver prices have risen by 5% and 7%, respectively.

According to Peter Schiff, price hikes in equities, gold, and silver indicate that Wall Street and traditional investors are celebrating the election outcome, marked by Democrats winning control of both the House and Senate.

Initially, investors feared a lengthy political battle after the Democratic sweep. However, traditional capital assets rebounded after Trump accepted the outcome, dispelling fears of an election dispute. In short, investors expect a divided Congress to clamp down on government spending and borrowing.

Also, the yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury note dropped by 4.91% following the Democratic victory. This means lower Treasury yields support stock valuations by reducing borrowing costs and eroding bond returns, making them less attractive relative to equities and precious metals. This explains strong gains in U.S. stocks and rare metals.

Bitcoin weakened after the midterm election, noting that the timing indicates that the vote and the subsequent Binance hack impacted investor sentiment. Today, BTC trades at $73,135, after losing a crucial support at $75,000 and falling from its recent $80,000 peak.

Schiff is aware that Bitcoin always falls after midterm elections. He knows more drops are coming now that the asset has lost its key support at $75k. #5189. BitGo Posts $44M Quarterly Profit as Platform Assets Grow, But Adjusted EBITDA Stays Negative

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: BitGo reported roughly $44.1 million in third-quarter net income even as adjusted EBITDA remained negative at about $4.3 million. Assets on its platform rose to $59.9 billion on the company’s normalized measure. The headline revenue figure includes substantial direct costs, so it should not be treated like a conventional software sales number.

BitGo’s third-quarter results offer a useful case study in why crypto-company earnings need more than a glance at the revenue line. The custody and infrastructure provider reported a positive net result, growing platform assets and continued expansion of its customer base. Yet one measure of ongoing profitability remained below zero.

In its earnings exhibit filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, the company reported net income of roughly $44.1 million and adjusted EBITDA of negative $4.3 million for the third quarter of 2026. Those two figures tell different stories because they do not include the same items.

Reported total revenue was approximately $2.85 billion, compared with around $5.81 billion in the comparable year-earlier quarter. At first glance that looks like an extraordinary contraction for a custody business. But BitGo also reported about $2.81 billion in direct costs against the latest revenue total.

The large figures reflect the accounting presentation of transaction-related activity, rather than pure software or recurring subscription income. The spread between revenue and direct costs is therefore an important part of understanding the economics. Comparing headline gross revenue with that of a conventional enterprise-software company could mislead readers.

The company attributed positive GAAP net income in part to treasury-related appreciation, while its adjusted EBITDA measure was still negative. Investors should examine those adjustments rather than assuming accounting profit automatically equals positive cash generation from ordinary operations.

BitGo said normalized assets on platform rose 31.9% to $59.9 billion and normalized staked assets grew 41.1%. It also cited approximately 6,640 clients. Those metrics provide a view into demand for its services even as fluctuations in transaction-related revenue complicate the income statement.

The distinction matters to institutions selecting custodians. A provider’s commercial footprint can expand while costs, pricing or exceptional items cause a temporary mismatch between headline earnings and adjusted operating profit. Conversely, assets under service are not the same as assets BitGo owns or can freely use.

NewsBTC recently described BitGo’s role in custody arrangements for a Grayscale-related Hyperliquid product. We also covered plans for BitGo to provide access to a WisdomTree tokenized Treasury product. Both illustrate why custody businesses compete on institutional integrations as well as transactional volume.

The figures reinforce the idea that crypto infrastructure companies are not interchangeable with the tokens they support. A higher Bitcoin price may lift the value of assets in custody, while trading patterns, service mix, expenses and treasury changes can pull reported results in different directions.

Normalized platform assets also depend on the company’s definition of that measure, which readers should consult in the filing. It is not identical to customer deposits at a bank and should not be used as a proxy for BitGo’s own balance-sheet cash.

The useful follow-ups will be whether client and staking activity translate into better margins, how much of future earnings comes from recurring custody services, and whether adjusted operating profitability improves. Any forward-looking forecast should be separated from the quarter’s actual results.

BitGo has shown growth in assets handled and a positive bottom-line accounting result. But the negative adjusted EBITDA means the operating-quality story is still more complicated than a single profit headline might suggest.

#5186. HIVE Reports $84.9M Revenue as AI GPU Business Grows 71% Amid Mining Pressures

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: HIVE Digital reported $84.9 million in fiscal second-quarter revenue and roughly 71% growth in its AI-focused BUZZ GPU business. The company also recorded a substantial quarterly loss, including a mining-equipment impairment. The results show both the promise and cost of shifting computing capacity toward AI services.

Bitcoin miners have spent much of 2026 trying to turn their access to electricity, land and data centers into businesses that can serve more than one market. HIVE Digital’s latest numbers put a price tag on that strategy.

The company said its fiscal second quarter, ended September 30, 2026, brought in approximately $84.9 million of revenue. Its BUZZ high-performance-computing division generated about $8.8 million, an increase of 70.7% from the comparable period. HIVE also reported about $139 million in cash on the balance sheet.

The growth is meaningful, but the AI arm remains far smaller than the company’s combined operations. A rapidly growing new division does not automatically replace the economics of Bitcoin mining.

HIVE reported a quarterly net loss in the region of $78 million and included a mining-equipment impairment of approximately $31.2 million. Impairments are generally noncash accounting charges in the period they are recorded, but they can still indicate that expected future economic value has fallen.

That distinction is important. A loss containing a major impairment is not the same as the business spending an identical amount of cash in the quarter. Equally, treating impairments as irrelevant would miss what they say about the pressure on older machines or assumptions about their earning potential.

Mining hardware has a useful life shaped by electricity prices, network difficulty, equipment efficiency and Bitcoin’s market value. When those assumptions change, a fleet that looked attractive two years ago may not justify its former carrying value.

The case for AI data centers is that demand for specialized computing may offer a revenue stream less closely tied to Bitcoin’s mining difficulty. But supplying GPU services requires capital, customer relationships, network infrastructure and operational expertise different from the work of running application-specific mining rigs.

NewsBTC has tracked miners making that transition, including Riot’s Bitcoin sales alongside its AI-data-center ambitions. HIVE’s BUZZ expansion is another version of the same strategic question: how quickly can an established miner earn durable income from compute services?

Partnerships and infrastructure projects are relevant here too. Our reporting on TeraWulf’s growth in AI leasing shows how the business of securing power-intensive sites and monetizing them through leases has become competitive. Possessing a data center does not guarantee demand for the GPUs housed in it.

Future reports should clarify how much revenue the AI division earns, whether its margins justify continued capital investment and how the mining segment performs as difficulty changes. Total company revenue can rise or fall for reasons unrelated to the profitability of the new computing business.

Investors should also watch the company’s liquidity, debt commitments and equipment spending. The $139 million cash figure is helpful context, but not a substitute for understanding cash consumption and future construction obligations.

HIVE is presenting itself as a dual-engine business. The latest quarter demonstrates that GPU services are growing quickly, while the bottom-line loss shows why the transition remains a work in progress rather than an accomplished turnaround.

Hyperliquid has received another major boost, but the impact could be bigger than it initially appears.

Upbit has officially listed HYPE on their South Korean exchange. This is significant, as it means the largest crypto spot exchange in South Korea now holds HYPE. This gives traders in South Korea a massive new pool of liquidity. However, it’s Upbit’s dominance in South Korea that makes the listing even more significant.

According to FP Research, Upbit controlled a significant 68.6% of trading volume across the country’s top five major crypto exchanges in April 2026, much higher than Bithumb’s 19.5%. This gives HYPE access to South Korea’s largest crypto trading platform and a much wider pool of local investors.

Notably, though, Hyperliquid’s [HYPE] expansion into South Korea could be just the beginning.

Recently, Bitso, one of Latin America’s largest crypto exchanges, also added HYPE to its perpetual market. This is interesting since Upbit has a spot listing for HYPE. Put simply, Bitso increases HYPE’s exposure in derivatives, while Upbit provides increased exposure for HYPE to South Korean spot traders.

Together, these listings expand HYPE’s exposure into several new markets and trading segments. However, could the Upbit listing offer more value to Hyperliquid? On-chain activity shows that exposure to South Korea’s large spot market may attract some new buying interest and create increased spot liquidity to help reinvigorate the HYPE ecosystem.

Hyperliquid continues to lead the perp trading market, with competitors still struggling to close the gap.

According to DeFiLlama data, Hyperliquid saw more than $65 billion in perp volume this week alone, compared to Aster’s $11 billion. This shows how much of a commanding lead Hyperliquid has in derivatives. Meanwhile, Q4 perp volume has already reached nearly 50% of Q3’s $620 billion total, suggesting that trading activity on Hyperliquid remains strong despite broader market weakness.

Despite this, there is still plenty of growth left to come. Looking at the chart below, Hyperliquid has been averaging around $15 billion each quarter in spot trading volume this year. However, in Q3 2025 it hit $54 billion.

Looking at the gap between this and the derivatives volume in Q3 2025, which hit around $630 billion in perps, it is safe to say that Hyperliquid’s derivatives volume is almost 45x larger than Spot volume. In essence, Hyperliquid still depends heavily on derivatives activity to drive its on-chain momentum.

Against this backdrop, Upbit’s listing could put HYPE in a stronger position to close that gap. The opportunity to access South Korea’s big spot market opens up new buying opportunities, increasing spot liquidity, and helps diversify Hyperliquid’s trading activity beyond perpetual futures.

If this momentum continues, spot growth could become an important driver of the next phase of Hyperliquid’s ecosystem expansion.

Upbit’s 68.6% market share gives HYPE access to South Korea’s largest spot trading market.

With perp volume nearly 45 times larger than spot volume, Upbit’s listing could bring new buyers, boost spot activity and support HYPE’s growth.

#5182. NYSE Selects Avalanche for Tokenized Stock Settlement: Can AVAX Reclaim $9.00?

Home » Altcoins » NYSE Selects Avalanche for Tokenized Stock Settlement: Can AVAX Reclaim $9.00?

Wall Street’s tokenization push gives Avalanche an institutional boost, but AVAX technicals demand caution at important level.

In a major endorsement of enterprise blockchain infrastructure, the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) has chosen Avalanche (AVAX) technology as the core ledger for clearing and settling trades on its planned tokenized stock platform.

According to an Ava Labs statement, Avalanche will provide the core ledger technology for the clearing firm of the NYSE-affiliated digital trading platform.

Subject to regulatory approval, the platform is designed to enable 24/7 trading, clearing and onchain settlement of tokenized securities.

It will support equities issued across multiple blockchains, while Avalanche will provide the underlying settlement infrastructure, offering predictable performance and costs, controlled network access and regulatory flexibility.

The announcement comes amid intensifying competition in financial asset tokenization. The NYSE has expanded its transfer agent network to six firms, including Broadridge, Computershare and Superstate.

Nasdaq is also developing tokenized securities infrastructure, while DTCC launched its tokenization service in October, using a private Besu blockchain and the Canton Network.

Meanwhile, the SEC’s new innovation exemption is opening the door to tokenized equity trading, with OKX and ICE pursuing a separate initiative.

Following the announcement, AVAX broke out of its previous consolidation range but faced resistance at $8.80–$9.00, triggering a pullback. As of November 10, AVAX is trading at approximately $8.48, up 7.2% over 24 hours.

The rally pushed Bollinger Bands wider, signaling increased volatility. AVAX is now trading below the middle band at $8.62 and the moving-average reference at $8.56, suggesting that upward momentum has cooled.

Resistance stands at $8.60–$8.65 and $9.00–$9.28, while key support can be located around $8.00, followed by $7.70 and $7.30.

Over the next few days, AVAX’s direction will largely depend on whether buyers can reclaim $8.65.A recovery above $8.65 could put AVAX back on course to test $9.00. A break above $9.28, supported by stronger trading volume, would signal renewed bullish momentum.

Failure to regain near-term resistance could leave the token consolidating, while a break below $7.95 would expose lower support levels at $7.70 or $7.30.

The NYSE announcement strengthens Avalanche’s position in institutional tokenization, but its implications for AVAX remain less direct. The platform is expected to run on a dedicated blockchain built using Avalanche technology rather than the public Avalanche network.

The extent of any resulting demand for AVAX will depend on how the platform is implemented and whether it creates mechanisms for value to accrue to the token.

A sustained recovery could put $9.50–$10.00 within reach, with further resistance around $10.50–$11.50. However, failure to overcome overhead resistance could leave AVAX in a broader consolidation range.

The NYSE announcement is a significant development for Avalanche’s institutional prospects, but it has yet to translate into a confirmed bullish reversal for AVAX. After the initial AVAX price rally, traders are now assessing whether buying demand can sustain the move beyond the immediate resistance level.

Trump Media & Technology Group is in the news today after reporting a $409.7 million Q3 profit, reversing a $238.1 million loss in Q2. Gains on digital assets and equity securities drove the turnaround.

At the time of writing, DJT traded at $4.10, with its shares closing at $4.06 on 9th November, up 1.75% before the earnings release.

Trump Media recorded $496.1 million in combined gains on digital assets and equity securities. The largest contribution was a $200.8 million unrealized gain on Bitcoin [BTC] pledged for its Options strategy. By quarter-end, the company had pledged 11,385.20 BTC for that strategy.

Another $107.5 million came from unrealized gains on Bitcoin and Cronos [CRO] holdings.

Equity securities added about $118 million in realized and unrealized gains.

After derivatives losses and other investment items, it reported $60 million in net investment income. CFO Phillip Juhan linked that investment income to a rise in BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT).

This reflects the 42% increase in IBIT’s closing share price to roughly $47 on September 30th, from roughly $33 on June 30th.

Trump Media also used proceeds from a partial sale of its IBIT holdings to buy 4,359 BTC during the quarter.

The next test for Trump Media’s Bitcoin [BTC] holdings can come from its debt. Holders of up to $1 billion in convertible notes could demand cash repayment on 30th November.

According to Interim CEO Kevin McGurn, the company favors using cash and credit and wants to “preserve as much of our Bitcoin as possible.” Management also clarified that the amount holders would request remains uncertain.

Bitcoin also made up about half of the $718.5 million in collateral backing the notes at quarter-end. Bitcoin-related securities and restricted cash made up the rest.

On 5th November, two transfers moved about 4,259 BTC to Crypto.com from wallets Arkham labeled as note collateral. The total was close to the 4,260.73 BTC listed in the filing.

The repayment deadline falls before Trump Media’s shareholder vote on the proposed TAE Technologies merger on 14th December. TAE drew another $100 million from Trump Media on 7th October, after the quarter-end cash snapshot.

#5180. Bitdeer Revenue Jumps 89% to $320.7M as AI Backlog Grows Despite Quarterly Loss

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Bitdeer posted record third-quarter revenue of $320.7 million, up 89% year over year, while reporting a $125.5 million net loss. Its stated AI-cloud backlog approached $2.9 billion, highlighting demand potential but not revenue already earned or cash already collected.

Bitdeer has delivered one of the clearest examples yet of a Bitcoin mining business trying to transform itself into a provider of broader computing infrastructure. Its latest quarter brought record revenue and a sizable artificial-intelligence cloud order pipeline. It also remained deeply unprofitable under standard accounting measures.

In its November 10 third-quarter results announcement, the company reported $320.7 million in revenue, an 89% increase from the year-earlier period. Adjusted EBITDA rose to about $69.6 million, while the GAAP net loss reached approximately $125.5 million.

Those measures differ, and the gap requires careful reading. Management highlighted changes in the fair value of digital-asset-related borrowing, including a $54.6 million noncash item, as one factor in the accounting result.

The figure likely to attract the most attention is Bitdeer’s reported AI-cloud backlog of approximately $2.9 billion. A backlog represents contracted or expected future services under the company’s reporting definitions, rather than cash already received or recognized quarterly revenue.

The amount eventually converted into sales will depend on contract delivery, customer demand, capacity coming online and the terms attached to commitments. Investors should seek disclosures about timing and any conditions that could delay or reduce the total.

Nevertheless, a substantial backlog can signal customer interest for specialized infrastructure. That is particularly valuable in a business where constructing or equipping data centers involves significant upfront spending.

Bitdeer reported production of 3,855 Bitcoin during the quarter and said it held 47 Bitcoin at quarter-end. Those figures help distinguish operating output from Bitcoin retained on the balance sheet. Production can be high even if a firm sells most of the coins to fund operations, equipment or other projects.

The company also reported approximately $213.7 million in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash. A cash balance should be considered alongside capital commitments, financing costs and planned expansion rather than treated as unencumbered profits from AI.

NewsBTC has reported on Riot’s decision to sell Bitcoin as it pursues major AI infrastructure contracts. The miners are pursuing different projects, but both illustrate a sector balancing near-term funding needs with investments that may generate future revenue.

Our coverage of Soluna and Bitdeer’s Texas infrastructure agreement adds a concrete example of why access to powered sites and commercial partnerships remains important as the competition for computing capacity grows.

Adjusted EBITDA may help investors evaluate operating performance before certain expenses and valuation changes. It is not identical to net income or free cash flow. A company can report a positive adjusted measure and still incur losses, financing costs and heavy investment requirements.

That is why the $125.5 million net loss deserves to stand alongside the $320.7 million revenue headline. Both are true, and neither alone gives a complete picture.

Bitdeer’s next reporting periods need to show when AI-cloud backlog turns into delivered services, how those services contribute to margins and how much capital they consume. Improvements in mining efficiency and power costs will also remain relevant.

The latest results point to striking revenue momentum and a potentially meaningful new business line. They do not yet demonstrate that the shift toward AI has resolved the financial volatility historically associated with Bitcoin mining.

#5179. Don’t Store Crypto on iPhone, Ledger CTO Says

Ledger Chief Technology Officer Charles Guillemet has recently warned cryptocurrency holders not to store critical wallet information on their iPhones, as the security threat is on the rise.

In his recent post on X, the Ledger executive highlighted the fact that vulnerabilities that can leak important data are now becoming more and more accessible for hackers to exploit.

"Unfortunately this kind of vulnerability used to be very expensive and reserved to high potential attackers," Guillemet tweeted.

However, he pointed out that we're now on the verge of seeing the costs of such vulnerabilities go down to zero, meaning that it could become very easy for cybercriminals to exploit them on a massive scale.

"Simply don't store any valuable in your mobile. Especially not your crypto seeds," the Ledger CTO cautioned.

His words came in response to an urgent security alert published by crypto exchange Binance over a vulnerability that was found in Apple's iOS operating system.

In particular, cryptocurrency exchange Binance reported a vulnerability, dubbed worse_query, which can allow malicious applications to gain access to files of other applications installed on the same device.

As specified by the exchange, this security flaw affects iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1 and 27.2.

This means that crypto wallet recovery phrases, private keys and login credentials can be at risk, as they may be stored in accessible local files.

Binance underscored that this concern isn't exclusive to the exchange's app alone, while adding that the vulnerability can have an impact on the entire crypto space.

The exchange recommended that users uninstall apps that were downloaded from untrusted sources, update their operating systems and avoid installing any unauthorized software.

Binance also advised users to transfer their funds to newly created wallets on clean devices if they think their wallets may have been compromised.

Apple published new security updates on Nov. 9. However, it's not clear if they are enough to fully patch this vulnerability. Still, there have been no confirmed crypto thefts specifically linked to the exploit.

Guillemet's warning comes a month after Ledger's major security incident involving compromised hardware wallets.

Back in October, French cryptocurrency hardware wallet maker Ledger admitted that some hardware wallets distributed by its Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis had been tampered with.

It turned out that hackers managed to install complex hardware implants in legitimate Ledger devices. With that, hackers were able to intercept users' recovery phrases when people were setting up their Ledger wallets for the first time.

As shown by Ledger's investigation, malicious implants were capable of capturing the 24-word recovery phrase that appears on the Ledger device screen and then passing it to attackers via a cellular connection.

Blockchain sleuths estimated that this incident might have led to more than $86 million in crypto losses. However, Ledger itself didn't confirm the total amount.

#5176. eToro Q3 Profit Drops 74% as Crypto Trading Activity Slows

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: eToro reported third-quarter net income of about $15 million, down from $57 million a year earlier, as crypto-related activity weakened. Its funded-account base continued to grow, highlighting the difference between attracting customers and generating trading revenue from them in any particular quarter.

A trading platform can gain users even when the market becomes less profitable to trade. That tension runs through eToro’s latest financial results, which showed weaker quarterly earnings despite an expanding customer base.

According to the company’s November 10 earnings release, third-quarter net income was approximately $15 million, a decline of about 74% from $57 million in the comparable period. Net contribution came to around $186 million, down 13% year over year, with lower cryptocurrency trading activity contributing to the drop.

At the same time, eToro reported 4.39 million funded accounts, an increase of 18%, and assets under administration of approximately $20.8 billion. It also announced a $250 million share repurchase authorization.

Brokerage and trading businesses earn revenue from a mix of activity, product pricing and other services. When customers trade less frequently, a growing account base may not immediately offset the effect. The relationship is particularly visible in crypto, where transaction volumes can shift quickly as market sentiment changes.

That is why the funded-account figure and the net-contribution figure should be assessed together. One shows a measure of customer acquisition and retention; the other gives more insight into the contribution earned from services in the quarter.

Assets under administration are also distinct from eToro’s own cash and corporate assets. They reflect client-related asset values that can be affected by price movements as well as client activity.

Lower crypto activity at one trading platform does not prove digital assets are in a long-term decline. Users may trade through different venues, switch into other asset classes or simply become less active during a choppy period. The business may also earn different amounts from different types of orders.

Still, eToro’s numbers offer an operating-business perspective on the volatility seen in public-market crypto demand. NewsBTC has been tracking recent Bitcoin ETF outflows as well as uneven demand for spot Ether funds. ETF subscriptions and brokerage transaction revenues are separate metrics, but both help describe how investors are participating in the market.

A fall in net contribution can also reflect conditions in noncrypto products. Readers should avoid attributing every change in a diversified platform’s results to Bitcoin prices alone.

The $250 million repurchase authorization gives eToro permission to buy back shares under its program, subject to the company’s terms. It is not proof that the full amount was repurchased on November 10, nor does it guarantee future share-price gains.

Repurchases can alter the share count and capital allocation over time, but their effect depends on execution price, cash available and how the company balances other investments. They are best evaluated alongside earnings quality and strategic spending.

Investors should watch whether funded-account growth leads to sustained activity and improved net contribution in subsequent quarters. The product mix matters: strength in equities or other services could help offset a quieter crypto market, while increased marketing and operating costs could limit the benefit.

For crypto observers, the report is a reminder that adoption and profitability do not always move together. eToro gained funded accounts, but the softer trading environment made it harder to translate that scale into quarterly profit.

#5173. Coinbase, Kalshi, Kraken parent seek to back CFTC in stock perps fight

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Some of crypto’s biggest names are lining up behind the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in court. The fight is over whether Americans get to trade perpetual futures on individual stocks.

On the 9th of November, Coinbase, Kalshi, Kraken’s parent Payward, DRW Holdings, Jump Trading and Paradigm asked a federal judge to let them file a brief backing the CFTC.

What’s the fight about? The Capital Markets Alliance Association (CMAA) sued to undo the CFTC’s approval of single-stock perpetual futures.

These six companies think the CFTC got it right.

In the brief (shared by Coinbase’s legal representative Molly Abraham), they argue these products already fit under existing US futures laws. Thing is, the judge isn’t leaning their way so far.

Just days earlier, the court said the CFTC likely “exceeded its statutory authority” by letting these contracts trade as security futures.

So they’re jumping in while they’re behind.

Last week, the CFTC said stock perps could trade on US-regulated exchanges for the first time. Days later, the CMAA sued. This is a new trade group, and its members include Cboe and Citadel Securities.

The argument being made is that a contract with no end date isn’t a future. It’s a security-based swap, which puts it mainly under the SEC. It would also have to come with stricter limits on retail trading.

Not everyone agrees. Per Coinbase and team, nothing says a security future has to expire. This would keep these contracts under shared CFTC and SEC watch.

Judge Valerie Caproni is leaning toward the trade group for now. She said these look more like swaps. But she didn’t stop trading, since the group couldn’t show it faced urgent, lasting harm.

So stock perps stay live, for now. The trade group’s next filing is due on the 10th.

#5172. Bitcoin’s ‘best buying opportunity ever’ has arrived: Mark Moss

Bitcoin Opportunity Fund co-founder Mark Moss says that with banks and ETFs widening access to Bitcoin he expects a new record high in 2027.

Wall Street’s embrace of Bitcoin has created the “best buying opportunity ever,” according to investor Mark Moss.

Moss co-founded the Bitcoin Opportunity Fund, where he is an advisory partner. In 2025, UK-listed Satsuma Technology appointed him chief Bitcoin strategist.

Moss tells Cointelegraph on the latest episode of Trade Secrets that he first bought Bitcoin in 2015 at about $300, during a recovery from a $1,000 to $200 plunge.

“It was so risky,” Moss recalls of buying back then. In contrast, today, “you have consensus from the US government and Wall Street.”

“But most people still think it’s a scam,” he says.

That skepticism opens buying opportunities as Bitcoin starts to cross what Moss calls the “chasm” between early adopters and mainstream investors. Banks and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have made Bitcoin easier to buy and financial advisers could help persuade clients who have stayed away previously to consider investing.

Related: Strategy shareholders approve daily dividends for four preferred stocks

Bitcoin briefly climbed above $80,000 after the Democrats took control of the US Congress in the midterm elections, then gave back those gains as tech stocks sold off. By Friday, it fell to $74,762, its lowest level since August and remains in the doldrums at the time of writing.

Despite the selloff, Moss points to the reaction to the $6.3 billion Binance hack as a sign that sellers were running out.

Bitcoin fell to $76,320 after the breach and slid to $74,762 on Friday, erasing its post-election gains. It fell further to about $73,500 late Sunday, its lowest level since August, after Nvidia’s board announced it would investigate reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.

Bitcoin found another bottom after reports of Nvidia CEO’s scandal. Source: CoinMarketCap

Flows into US spot Bitcoin ETFs swung sharply during election week. The funds took in about $75 million on Wednesday, then shed $430 million on Thursday.

History is on the side of hodlers however. Bitcoin gained an average of about 53% in the 12 months after previous US midterms, Moss says, using data going back to 2014. That leaves three completed election cycles in his sample. He says he expects Bitcoin to set a new all-time high in 2027.

Moss thinks the Bitcoin treasury company to own is Strategy (MSTR), but believes that holding Bitcoin yourself is still superior. Strategy began buying Bitcoin in 2020 and turned those purchases into a core part of its business. It has used stock and debt sales to fund its purchases, giving investors a way to bet on Bitcoin through a publicly traded company.

By Nov. 2, Strategy held 849,327 BTC, more than 4% of Bitcoin’s maximum supply.

“I don’t think there’s another publicly traded company that will outperform Strategy over the next ten years,” Moss says.

Strategy has the world’s largest corporate Bitcoin trove. Source: BitcoinTreasuries.Net

Leverage can help a Bitcoin treasury company’s shares outperform the cryptocurrency it holds when its price rises.

But even if Strategy outperforms, Moss wouldn’t trade his Bitcoin holdings for its shares.

Related: 1inch lawyer sees agencies driving US crypto regulation as midterms unfold

Before Moss bought his first Bitcoin, he made a living buying foreclosed properties, fixing them up and selling them. He moved into property development, then built and sold a medical equipment business. He says he put the proceeds into Southern California real estate.

When the market crashed in 2008, he lost it all.

“The reward of being right is not worth the risk of getting it wrong,” he says.

Even with his outlook for Strategy, Moss says he’d keep his Bitcoin and use only a small share of his portfolio to pursue higher returns through treasury stocks.

In Moss’s model, Bitcoin could reach $1 million under certain circumstances, when it competes with stocks, bonds, gold and real estate for a considerable share of investors’ wealth. The model estimates how much those assets are worth, projects how that pool could grow as the global money supply expands and calculates a Bitcoin price based on the share it captures.

Financial advisers could help bring in that money via one client’s portfolio at a time, encouraging them to shift a few percentage points out of stocks or bonds and into Bitcoin. The scenario depends on a critical mass of clients doing that, to the point where all those small allocations add up.

The model also assumes Bitcoin stays secure and decentralized. Asked what could derail the scenario, Moss pointed to a failure that compromised either feature.

Moss says $1 million is possible by 2030... though hodler’s might have to wait until 2032.

#5171. Exodus Reports $8.3M Quarterly Loss as Wallet Platform Expands Payments Business

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Exodus reported third-quarter revenue of around $32.5 million, up 7%, while swinging to an $8.3 million net loss from a profit a year earlier. The wallet company’s expansion into payments and card infrastructure adds a new commercial opportunity but also increases the importance of integration costs and execution.

Exodus built its brand around software that helps people hold and exchange digital assets without relying on a traditional centralized exchange account. Its latest results show that running a wallet business at scale now involves more than downloads and token swaps.

In its November 9 third-quarter report, Exodus said revenue reached about $32.5 million, an increase of roughly 7% year over year. The company nevertheless recorded a net loss of approximately $8.3 million, compared with a net profit of about $17 million a year earlier.

The difference between higher revenue and weaker net income points to costs and accounting items that require as much attention as transaction volume.

Exodus reported around 1.4 million monthly active users and approximately 1.4 million quarterly funded users, reflecting the scale of its consumer product. Those are company-defined measures and may overlap; they should not be added together to imply a larger distinct customer base.

The company also cited roughly $1.1 billion in quarterly swap volume. Transaction volume measures value moved through a service; it is not the same as revenue or profit. The share retained by a platform depends on fees, execution arrangements and the costs of providing the service.

This is a useful distinction across the wallet industry. A product can support heavy activity without retaining a large percentage of the value exchanged. Increased usage can even create more customer-service, compliance and technical costs.

Exodus has been extending its role in the infrastructure around digital payments. Its recent company updates describe a combination involving Baanx and Monavate and a growing emphasis on card and payment services. It has also referenced around 1.6 million active cards and substantial payment volume in the broader business context.

Payment services offer a way to make digital assets useful for routine spending rather than only investment and exchange. But building or combining regulated payment operations brings operational work: issuing relationships, settlement partners, compliance programs, fraud controls and support obligations.

NewsBTC previously covered Visa’s work on stablecoin treasury and settlement infrastructure. Exodus operates in a different part of the market, yet both stories show businesses looking for ways to make digital value move through established financial channels.

Likewise, the growing attention paid to tokenized securities infrastructure reflects a wider focus on how blockchain assets connect with ordinary financial workflows. Neither development should be mistaken for proof that Exodus’s specific payment plans will succeed.

Management cited increased general and administrative spending among the pressures on the quarter. As a company moves from a comparatively focused software product toward a broader financial-services platform, staffing, oversight and integration costs can rise before new lines generate consistent returns.

That does not make the strategy inherently flawed. It means the outcome will depend on whether additional services create more durable recurring earnings than they cost to build and operate.

The useful measures in future results will include transaction and card activity, net revenue retained from those services, the cost of operating the expanded business and whether losses narrow. Users and investors should also pay attention to security, custody arrangements and regulatory disclosures as more payment services are introduced.

Exodus is showing modest revenue growth alongside a more expensive operating model. The next several quarters will help determine whether its payments ambitions create a stronger business or simply add complexity to an already competitive wallet market.

Declining liquidity in the market, weakening speculative interest, lackluster institutional interest and general macroeconomic conditions are all major factors causing most major altcoins to underperform so far.

#5169. Ripple CEO: Big XRP Holdings Don’t Mean Control

Home » Ripple (XRP) » Ripple CEO: Big XRP Holdings Don’t Mean Control

Security measures within XRP’s native ledger ensure no holder on the rich-list gets to take over the chain.

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse used the company’s Swell 2026 event to address a long-running claim that Ripple Labs effectively controls the XRP Ledger simply because it holds a large amount of XRP. He said ownership of the token does not confer authority over network rules or validation.

The XRP Ledger currently has more than 150 validators. Of the 35 on the current recommended unique node list, only one is operated by Ripple, roughly 2.9 percent.

Network operators decide which validators they trust and can configure their own lists rather than relying solely on any single published set.

Unlike proof-of-stake systems, XRP holdings do not grant extra voting weight. Independent validators reach agreement on transactions. Protocol amendments require at least 80 percent validator support for two consecutive weeks before they activate.

BOOOM! $XRP Holders🚨🚨🚨 @bgarlinghouse CEO of Ripple debunked one of the biggest misconceptions about XRP ledger!For everyone still claiming Ripple controls the XRP Ledger because it owns billions of XRP, listen to what Brad said at Ripple Swell 2026.Owning XRP does not… https://t.co/zyDgmkPmIM pic.twitter.com/mhpDrqLnXG

Ripple can propose software changes and invest in the ecosystem, but it cannot unilaterally force upgrades.

Three amendments have been activated this year: Permissioned Domains on February 4, Permissioned DEX on February 18, and Batch transactions on October 9, 2026.

Notably, these tools are designed to support more controlled environments for institutional applications while still operating on the shared ledger.

Several highly established financial firms have moved forward with XRP-related products. Aviva Investors launched a tokenized share class of its Sterling Liquidity Fund. Franklin Templeton, DBS Bank, and Ripple have outlined plans involving tokenized fund shares and RLUSD.

Standard Chartered has also announced live institutional custody of RLUSD on the ledger, with additional collateral work planned alongside Ripple and LMAX Group.

These bullish developments do not depend on Ripple controlling the ledger. They rely on the existing consensus rules, low transaction costs, and the ability of independent parties to issue assets and settle on the network.

Even without control of validation, XRP retains specific functions on the ledger. Transaction fees, currently as low as 0.00001 XRP, are destroyed. Funded accounts require a base reserve.

The OG token can also serve as an intermediary asset for bridging different issued currencies when that path offers better execution.

Mr. Garlinghouse’s comments restate a technical distinction that has been part of XRPL design for years: large XRP holdings do not equal governance power.
